title: Ask on Demand: Targeted Peer Communication for Parallel Agentic Systems
title_zh: 按需提问：面向并行智能体系统的定向同伴通信

paragraphs.en: 提出Ask on Demand框架，使并行智能体按需向同伴定向检索信息，提升性能并降低推理成本。 Parallel LLM agents tackle complex tasks by exploring multiple trajectories, yet useful discoveries remain isolated in individual execution histories. Existing sharing methods often select or summarize information before other agents' needs become clear, potentially overlooking details that become important later. We propose Ask on Demand (AOD), a communication framework that enables agents to seek targeted peer assistance when specific information needs arise. Upon an approved request, AOD retrieves relevant evidence from peer execution histories, selects a suitable peer, and generates a response tailored to the request. To determine when such assistance is worthwhile, we train a lightweight gate using paired team continuations, with supervision derived from final team outcomes and inference cost. Experiments on AppWorld and WebShop demonstrate that AOD consistently improves task performance over independent parallel execution while achieving lower inference cost than existing information-sharing baselines. These findings highlight the benefits of aligning peer communication with agents' evolving information needs to achieve more effective and efficient collaboration.
paragraphs.zh: 提出Ask on Demand框架，使并行智能体按需向同伴定向检索信息，提升性能并降低推理成本。并行LLM智能体通过探索多条轨迹来处理复杂任务，然而有用的发现仍孤立地存在于各自的执行历史中。 现有的共享方法往往在其他智能体的需求尚不明确时就选择或总结信息，可能忽略那些后来变得重要的细节。 我们提出Ask on Demand（AOD），这是一个通信框架，使智能体在出现特定信息需求时能够寻求针对性的同伴协助。 在请求获得批准后，AOD从同伴的执行历史中检索相关证据，选择合适的同伴，并生成针对该请求定制的回复。 为了判断此类协助何时值得进行，我们使用成对的团队延续数据训练一个轻量级门控，其监督信号来自最终团队结果与推理成本。 在AppWorld和WebShop上的实验表明，AOD持续优于独立并行执行的任务性能，同时推理成本低于现有的信息共享基线。 这些发现凸显了将同伴通信与智能体不断演进的信息需求相匹配的好处，从而实现更有效、更高效的协作。
